problem_statement:
When debugging multithreaded applications, there is no way to determine which thread produced a given log message. The current logging subsystem does not support including thread identification in log output.

For applications with APIs callable from multiple threads, knowing the originating thread is essential for debugging. For example, a Bluetooth stack may have separate RX, TX, and main threads all logging through the same module — without thread context, correlating log messages to execution flow is impossible.

The logging subsystem needs:
1. A Kconfig option (CONFIG_LOG_THREAD_ID_PREFIX) to enable thread ID storage in log messages
2. The log message structure must be extended to carry the thread ID (tid) of the calling thread
3. The log output formatting layer must support rendering the thread ID prefix
4. When CONFIG_THREAD_NAME is also enabled, the thread name should be shown instead of a raw pointer

Expected output format with the feature enabled:
  <err> [main] module: Error message
  <inf> [sysworkq] bt_hci_core: TX process start
  <dbg> [BT RX] bt_att: tx_meta_data_alloc: disabling timeout

The changes span the log message structure, the output formatting layer, and the backend standard header.

See: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/61410

verification.reason: The statement captures the feature but omits the new public API signature and flag that the hidden tests directly require; these can be added without revealing the implementation.

problems.detail: The hidden tests call log_output_process() with an extra const k_tid_t tid argument, but the statement does not specify that this public API gains a tid parameter or its position.
The hidden tests use LOG_OUTPUT_FLAG_THREAD, but the statement does not name this flag or explain that it requests thread ID prefix rendering.

The hidden tests check the exact rendered thread prefix for CONFIG_THREAD_NAME and for the non-thread-name case, so the statement needs to state that the formatter prints the thread name or raw pointer as the prefix.

leak_check.leak_detail: The statement mentions that the changes span the log message structure, output formatting layer, and backend standard header, and that the log message structure must carry tid. These hint at internal files/structures, but they do not reveal the algorithm or public interface details needed by the tests.
leak_check.suggested_statement:
When debugging multithreaded applications, there is no way to determine which thread produced a given log message. The current logging subsystem does not support including thread identification in log output.

For applications with APIs callable from multiple threads, knowing the originating thread is essential for debugging. For example, a Bluetooth stack may have separate RX, TX, and main threads all logging through the same module — without thread context, correlating log messages to execution flow is impossible.

The logging subsystem needs:
1. A Kconfig option (CONFIG_LOG_THREAD_ID_PREFIX) to enable thread ID storage in log messages
2. The logging subsystem must make the calling thread ID available to the output formatting layer
3. The log output formatting layer must support rendering the thread ID prefix
4. When CONFIG_THREAD_NAME is also enabled, the thread name should be shown instead of a raw pointer

The public log_output_process() function must be extended with an additional `const k_tid_t tid` parameter, located after the `const char *source` parameter and before the `uint8_t level` parameter. A new log output bit flag macro `LOG_OUTPUT_FLAG_THREAD` must be defined. When CONFIG_LOG_THREAD_ID_PREFIX is enabled and LOG_OUTPUT_FLAG_THREAD is set in the flags passed to log_output_process(), the formatting layer must render the thread prefix after the level prefix and before the source/domain name. If CONFIG_THREAD_NAME is enabled, render the thread name; otherwise render the thread ID pointer using %p.

Expected output format with the feature enabled:
  <err> [main] module: Error message
  <inf> [sysworkq] bt_hci_core: TX process start
  <dbg> [BT RX] bt_att: tx_meta_data_alloc: disabling timeout

See: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/61410
